title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-07-11
lineage: AUD > MC > Cass > Cass > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Rare July‑11 1970 Fillmore East show with strong acoustic set and soaring Morning Dew, captured on a rough audience tape that loses the right channel for the first half.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised – Jerry’s pedal‑steel work, an early “So Sad” acoustic rendition, a spirited Rosa Lee debut and a thunderous Morning Dew make this a must‑hear night. The recording is an old‑school audience tape with left‑only audio for the first nine songs and noticeable hiss, but its historic value outweighs the technical flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rave about the musical moments (Morning Dew, So Sad, Rosa Lee) and give high performance scores, while recording complaints are consistent but not severe enough to outweigh the show’s rarity.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Left channel only for first nine tracks, tape hiss throughout, overall crude stone‑age sound; still usable because of rare acoustic set and historic context.

standout_songs: So Sad (To Watch Good Love Go Bad)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic segment opens with Easy Wind and includes rare Everly Brothers cover "So Sad" plus three gospel numbers, followed by a high‑energy electric set that builds to a powerful Morning Dew.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Highlighted for pedal‑steel on the acoustic side and heavy lead guitar throughout; possible early wah‑wah usage noted.
band_member_comments.Bob: Sings Good Lovin' and contributes vocal harmonies in the electric set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen is heard on keyboards (no vocals) during his solo segment.
